# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Xft text (`XftDrawStringUtf8`) | Xft text (XJack) |
| Threads, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first. A speed-up in the shared GL
layer counts too, even when every pinned frame hash still matches (HexTrail's
deferred depth clear): ask before writing it, and name it in the PR body.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. A hack that runs at a good rate
can still go: Rod dropped Boing (8.3 fps, "pretty boring on a small screen")
and asked for HexTrail to be tuned because it fell under 10 fps before the
rotation moved on. Judge a hack on a 466 px round screen, and by its worst
window as well as its mean. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |
| "Single precision is done, so the hack is as fast as it gets" | HexTrail gained 0.3 fps from it and 2.3 from a depth clear in the GL layer. Read what the shared code does each frame. |
| "The mean is above 10 fps" | HexTrail's mean was 15.3 and its worst window 10.8; its step grew all cycle. Read the lowest window. |

# Porting a batch of hacks

For several hacks on one branch, with Rod away. The per-hack steps are in
`SKILL.md` and `adding-a-hack.md`; this is what a batch adds. Per-hack findings
live in `.claude/rules/hacks.md`, not here.

## Order of work

1. Read every header before copying anything: a `(GPL)` tag or an xlock notice
   changes the notices row, and a licence that is not a permission notice means
   stop and ask.
2. Triage by gap count. Do the easy ones first: they pay for shim gaps the
   others need. Leave GL and anything under a few fps to last.
3. One branch, a commit per hack, shim code test-first and mutation-checked.
   No PR until Rod says.
4. `uv run tools/wire_hack.py <name> <Class> "<copyright>"` copies the file and
   registers it with a frame hash of `0` (skipped), so every commit stays green.
   Then `pio run -e dump`, fill the gaps, dump frames at several counts and
   look at them.
5. Flash and measure each hack as soon as it runs
   (`bash tools/flash_and_capture.sh <hack> 30`). Report measured, unjudged and
   unseen separately.
6. Pin all the new hashes in one run, after looking at the frames:
   `HACK_PINS_OUT=<file> pio test -e native -f test_hacks`.
7. Soak the whole registry before handing over: `-DROTATE_SECONDS=5` for five
   laps, then look for a reboot, a panic or a "Stack canary", and compare PSRAM
   on each visit of the new hacks (it should match exactly).
8. Measured rows, rules, a regenerated assessment, and a notes file for Rod: what
   to look at, which choices are his, what was not measured. His review changes
   the numbers (a hack dropped, one retuned), so rewrite the notes after it or
   put the final state in the PR body, which is the record. A stale notes file
   misleads.

## Traps

| Trap | Do |
| --- | --- |
| A change that is not pixel-identical by construction (single precision, a faster fill) and you only checked fps | Look at a frame. A hack drew garbage for hours at "20 fps" |
| `#define double float` before a header that has `double` in a struct a shim `.c` shares | Include that header first, then the define; a flat-screen test guards it |
| A hack that keeps state in statics across starts | Its pin depends on earlier tests; reset the static in a wrapper, and test both outcomes |
| A mode picked with `random()` | A boot is deterministic, so measure the other mode by forcing it |
| Constants in pixels or frames, tuned for another window size or frame rate | Scale them at build time (`tools/fireworkx_patch.py`), not by editing the copy |
| A hack that treats `malloc(0) == NULL` as out of memory | The board returns NULL for zero bytes, the host a pointer: it stops drawing on the board only. Reproduce with an allocator hook that fails for zero |
| A stop that leaks | `MallocStackLogging=1 leaks --atExit -- .pio/build/dump/program <index> 0 out.raw` names the line (rebuild `-e dump` first) |

## Finding the cost

Skip one thing behind a temporary flag and read `step=`; revert it. Guessing
was wrong three times running. The usual causes here:

- full-frame passes over PSRAM: a clear, a copy, a blur, a 565 conversion (render
  smaller, alias a pixmap to the window, erase only what was drawn)
- the shim's polygon fill, which divides in double (`hacks/float_polygon.h`)
- soft double: `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm <object> | grep ' U __.*df'`; `frand` hides
  a `1.0` in its macro body (`hacks/single_frand.h`)
- a pause the hack asks for (`wait=`): override `*delay` and say the pace changed
- a GL hack's clear and push, which scale with the dirty box, and work the GL
  layer does that nothing reads (a depth clear with the depth test off):
  `gl_budget.py` shows vertices submitted against triangles drawn

## Choices for Rod

When look and speed trade off, leave a build flag per option, measure each, and
register the one nearer his bar. After his hands-on notes, expect to retune or
drop: from seven ports he kept six and dropped Boing, and asked for HexTrail to
be faster. Keep a flashable rotation build ready (`-DROTATE_SECONDS=25`, the new
hacks first) and say which build the board holds when you stop.

## Tools

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Register a hack | `tools/wire_hack.py` |
| Flash a pinned build and read the serial log | `tools/flash_and_capture.sh`, `tools/serial_capture.py` |
| Does a test notice a break | `tools/mutate.py <file> 'old=>new' --cmd '...'` |
| Pin hashes | `HACK_PINS_OUT` (above) |
# Adding a hack

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md. The order of work is in `SKILL.md`.

The `port-hack` skill orders this work, says what to read for before copying a
hack, and holds a recipe per trap. The steps:

1. Check its row in `docs/porting-assessment.md` (effort and Speed band) and
   read its licence header.
2. Update the expected list in `firmware/test/test_hacks/test_hacks.c` and see
   it fail.
3. Copy the file to `firmware/src/hacks/<name>/<name>.c`, add the notices row
   and an `extern` plus entry in `hacks/registry.c`.
4. Fill shim gaps test-first in `firmware/test/test_xshim/`. The compile
   check in `score_hacks.py` shows what is missing.
5. Host tests pass, dump a frame and look at it, then (with Rod's go-ahead)
   flash and measure fps and free heap/PSRAM over serial. To pin its frame
   hash after looking at the frame, put `0x1ull` in `kBaseline`, run
   `pio test -e native -f test_hacks`, convert the "Was N" in the failure line
   with `python3 -c "print(hex(N))"`, and run it again.
6. Regenerate the assessment and add measurements to
   `tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, then re-run the speed backtest: each port
   adds a point to the check of the Speed bands, which were fitted to the first
   29 hacks. To make a port a real test, commit its host time and predicted
   range first (`docs/speed-predictions.md` shows the form), flash it as copied,
   and add its name to `HOLDOUT` in `tools/speed_backtest.py`. The first four
   (Mountain, Epicycle, Kaleidescope, Celtic) all fell where predicted.
7. If a hack is slow and `double`-heavy (many `double`s, `sqrt`, `sin`/`cos`,
   `pow`), try a single-precision wrapper like `hacks/galaxy_single.c` (for a
   plain screenhack, `hacks/substrate_single.c`; the recipe is in the skill's
   `techniques.md`), and compare double and float frames at several frame
   counts. A resource
   override can skip a hack's restart cleanup: Galaxy leaked at `count: 2`, so
   leak-test any override.
8. If Rod drops a port after seeing it (Hypnowheel, Boing; Celtic was dropped
   and came back through issue #37): remove it
   from `g_hacks[]`, the expected list, its hash and its leak test; keep the
   source and notices row; add `name: reason` (short: it is printed as a
   bullet) to `tools/failed_ports.txt`. For a GL hack, keep the `<name>_gl.c`
   wrapper but exclude it and the directory (`-<hacks/boing/>
   -<hacks/boing_gl.c>`) in all three `build_src_filter` lines, or it still
   builds. A reason Rod gave in his own words ("boring on a small screen") is
   the reason to record. File an issue only if there is something to come back
   to.
   Unhook its build steps too: its entry in `patch_float_literals.py` and any
   pre-script only it needs (BlockTube's `gl_textures.py`), or every build
   still runs them and fails without their `vendor/` input.
9. A header that a pre-script writes into the build dir (the font, the grab
   image) must be included under `__has_include` in `native/dump_main.c`:
   `tools/probe_hacks.py` compiles that file without the build's generated
   directory, and an unconditional include failed two `test_probe_hacks`
   cases. Add the pre-script to all three `extra_scripts` lines in
   `platformio.ini`, and a wrapper's original source to all three
   `build_src_filter` lines (`sed -i.bak 's|<last entry>$|<last entry> <new>|'`

# Working in a git worktree

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

- In a git worktree the ignored `vendor/`, `.venv/` and `.platformio/` are
  missing. Symlink them from the main checkout. `.gitignore`'s trailing slashes
  don't match symlinks, so they would show as untracked, but the shared
  `.git/info/exclude` already lists the three names. That file is shared by
  every worktree: ask Rod before adding to it.
  The harness refuses `source tools/env.sh` and a computed `PATH` there: run
  `PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR=<worktree>/.platformio ../.venv/bin/pio ...` instead,
  and keep commands plain (no scripts, loops, `$VAR` in a command or `&&`
  chains with a computed path). A worktree an agent works in (`isolation:
  "worktree"`) starts from `origin/main`, not from your branch, and has no
  vendor or toolchain until you link them.
  It also refuses heredocs, `git -C` and `cd` into another worktree: use the
  Edit and Write tools. It refuses `git ... | tar` and `cd <dir> && git ...`
  too: use `git archive -o f.tar <sha>` then `tar -x -f f.tar -C <dir>`, and run
  git from the worktree root. A background shell starts there as well, so use
  `pio test -d <abs>/firmware` with absolute paths. Parallel calls can race
  (a `uv run` in the root disturbed `.venv` while `pio` ran:
  "../.venv/bin/pio: no such file"), so run
  `uv` and `pio` one at a time. To fast-forward `main` or remove the worktree,
  leave it first with `ExitWorktree keep`.
  Before `ExitWorktree remove` on a merged branch, check
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> origin/main`; the tool's "discarded N
  commits" count ignores merges. `.platformio`, `.venv` and `vendor` there are
  symlinks, so removal leaves the real ones alone. After a merge,
  `ExitWorktree keep` names a branch (`worktree-<name>`) that may not exist:
  remove the worktree with `git worktree remove --force <path>` and delete the
  real branch, as separate commands, because a failed `&&` link skips the rest
  silently. Check `git worktree list` afterwards. In a session resumed from a
  summary, `ExitWorktree` is a no-op ("no active EnterWorktree session"):
  remove the worktree with `git worktree remove --force <path>` from the main
  checkout instead. To delete the merged branch
  you are standing on, `git switch --detach origin/main` in the worktree first.
  The shell's directory resets after each command and after `ExitWorktree`, so
  use absolute paths (`../.venv/bin/pio` failed from the wrong place and the run
  looked like a test failure). A loop over several mutations is refused as a
  command: write it as a script in the scratchpad that edits the file, runs
  `pio test` through `subprocess` and restores the file in `finally`, then run
  it with `python3 -I`.
  Stopping such a script (TaskStop) kills it before `finally` runs: check
  `git diff` afterwards and restore the file by hand.
  Also refused: a heredoc (use the Write tool for a scratchpad script), `$(...)`
  inside a git command, and the quoted `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS` above combined
  with a redirect or `NO_COLOR=1`. Flashing worked as
  `PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR=<wt>/.platformio PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS="..."
  .venv/bin/pio run -d firmware -e stopwatch -t upload` with no redirect: the
  540 KB of output lands in a tool-results file, so grep that for "Hash of data
  verified". Edit and Write refuse the main checkout's path while you are in a
  worktree. `pio test -f test_x` runs the whole suite (`test_hacks` takes 3
  minutes, the full native run 7), and a failing summary reads "2 failed, 101
  succeeded": match `[FAILED]` or the return code, not "succeeded".

67	  `patch_float_literals.py`, which refuses it.
68	- Once the maths is float, look at the fills before the next idea. CWaves'
69	  cosines were 4 ms of a 61 ms step; its 233 column fills were 57 (a thin
70	  full-height rectangle touches a new cache line a store). See `hacks.md`.
71	- A float build can break a check that held in double. Both the S3 (`madd.s`)
72	  and arm64 fuse a multiply and an add, so `t*n - floor(t*n)` uses the exact
73	  product for the subtraction and the rounded one for the `floor`, and can
74	  come out slightly negative: Celtic's `assert(tt>=0 && tt<1)` aborted at
75	  t 0.331093 with 3422 segments. The 3000-frame test (`pio test`) found it
76	  on the host, and the same abort would have hit the board. Compute the
77	  product once in a build-time patch (`tools/celtic_patch.py`). Map any libm
78	  call the hack makes that `single_precision.h` does not (`rint`, `floor`),
79	  and check the object with `nm` for `__*df*` helpers, not only `__muldf3`.
80	
81	## Slow hack
82	
83	When: a ported hack runs under about 10 fps and the push is not the cause
84	(`step` in the serial line is large).
85	
86	- For a GL hack, flash a `-DGL_PROFILE` build first (AGENTS.md): it splits
87	  the frame into stages, and time in none of them is the hack's own code.
88	  Issue #73 guessed Hypnowheel was 70 percent blended fill; the profile showed
89	  a third of its frame was `double` trig.
90	- A worst-case microbenchmark is not the workload. A PSRAM cache miss costs
91	  about 220 cycles, which suggested GL fill was memory-bound; a banded renderer
92	  in internal RAM, built on that, was exact and slower (neighbouring triangles
93	  share cache lines). A/B the first working slice of a speed idea on the board
94	  before building the rest, and stop if it does not pay.
95	- Do not trust a host profile (`sample` on the dump program) for where the
96	  time goes. A Mac does `double` at full speed, so software-double code looks
97	  cheap there: Braid's disc fill was 6% on the host and the largest cost on the
98	  board.
99	- Split the step on the device with a temporary build flag that makes the
100	  expensive call return at once (Braid: `XDrawLine`). The step left is the
101	  hack's own cost; the difference is the drawing. Remove the flag before
102	  committing.
103	- Count what is called per frame (segments, calls, rows) before guessing,
104	  and look at the object file for soft-double helpers (see "Single precision").
105	- Change one thing, pin that the pixels did not move (`cmp` frames at several
106	  counts, or the pinned hash), flash, and compare second windows. Braid's four
107	  changes were worth 2.7-3.2 times, 1.05, and 1.3.
108	- Wide lines (`line_width` above 1) are the costly path: a quad filled a row at
109	  a time, plus two discs for round caps. `stroke.c` keeps a table of disc rows
110	  by width up to 16. A wide full circle through `XDrawArc` is about a thousand
111	  such segments (Deluxe: 94% of a frame, 2-5 fps); `stroke_circle` fills it as
112	  a ring in two spans a row.
113	- When the cost is overpaint, not `double` maths, a host split does find the
114	  dominant call: `#define XDrawArc(...) 0` in the wrapper, `pio run -e dump`,
115	  then `/usr/bin/time -p .pio/build/dump/program <index> 400 out.raw` three
116	  times, against the baseline. It cannot see costs that live in memory
117	  traffic (Deluxe's alpha mask: nothing on the host, 3-5 ms on the board).
118	- Counting works where timing misleads: a scratch copy of the hack with a
119	  counter in the inner function and a macro round `XDrawLine` gave Celtic's
120	  spline evaluations and line draws per draw call on the host, by graph type.
121	  A cost per eval and per line fitted to a first device capture (about 1.7 us
122	  and 22 us, from three graph types and a handful of windows) estimated 63 ms
123	  for the biggest type after the change; the next capture's 12.6-76.8 ms did
124	  not contradict it, but the log does not say which type each window was, so
125	  the fit is unchecked.
126	- A hack's own pacing constants can be the lever: Celtic's 0.0001 tick (a
127	  patch scales it, `CELTIC_STEP_SCALE`) set both the look-ahead's work and how
128	  many draw calls a picture takes. Count the draw calls a picture takes and
129	  the pause after it before reading `fps=`: with a 5 s pause the column read
130	  5.2 in every window and measured the pause, not the drawing. Use
131	  `1000 / (step + push + delay)` for the drawing rate.
132	- Heap and speed were two problems in Celtic and one fix cured only the
133	  first: the graph sized to the screen cut a pattern's heap about 9 times and
134	  left spline evaluations per call unchanged. Measure both after each change.
135	- A hack that redraws its whole picture every frame to animate colour (Braid)
136	  costs its full draw each frame whatever the push does. Check this before
137	  porting; the scorer does not flag it yet.
138	- A fix that moves the frame rate by under 5% shows the maths was not the
139	  cost. HexTrail in single precision went from 12.7 to 13.0 fps; the 2.3 fps
140	  that mattered came from reading what the GL layer does each frame
141	  (`glshim_clear`) and finding a depth clear that nothing read, because the hack
142	  never enables the depth test. Run `nm` on the object, then read the shared
143	  code the hack calls before trying a third idea in the hack.
144	- A step that grows over the hack's cycle (HexTrail: 19 ms to a ceiling, then it
145	  restarts) needs the worst window, not the mean. Capture at least one full
146	  cycle (150 s covered HexTrail's 65 s), read the lowest `fps=`, and compare the
147	  time spent below 10 fps with the rotation interval: Rod saw it fall under 10
148	  before the 25 s change. If a resource such as `count` scales the cost, give it
149	  an `#ifndef` default in `registry.c` (`HEXTRAIL_COUNT`) so one flash tests
150	  another value, and measure two or three values: count 6 gave a mean of 12.7,
151	  10 gave 9.1 and 20 gave 5.7, in double precision.
152	
153	## Thin lines in a GL hack
154	
155	When: a GL hack draws hairlines or fades (Unknown Pleasures) and looks right
156	in a host frame but flickers on the board. Work down this list, one layer at a
157	time, and look at the screen (or film) after each; each layer hid the next.
158	
159	- Lines hop. TinyGL snaps every vertex to a whole pixel, so a drifting line
160	  jumps. `tinygl_patch.py` keeps the fractional position and draws a Wu line
161	  when the hack enables `GL_LINE_SMOOTH`. Triangles are still snapped.
162	- Quads that hide the lines behind them hide nothing, or the picture is
163	  speckled grey. TinyGL's blend adds colours, ignores alpha and misreads our
164	  byte-swapped pixels, so `SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` is drawn as an
165	  opaque fill. Smooth lines carry no alpha, so a hack's per-line fade is lost.
166	- A line drawn on its own polygon's edge is erased in dashes: `glPolygonOffset`
167	  was stored and never read. The patch applies it, plus a margin for the
168	  vertex snapping. Check the effect on the host by the second difference of a
169	  frame's total brightness while the picture drifts a fraction of a pixel; change
170	  one thing at a time, because blending once made the experiment unable to
171	  show any effect.
172	- Pieces of a line vanish for one refresh. The panel scans while the push
173	  writes, so a seam crosses the picture. Set `sync_to_refresh` on the hack
174	  (`XLOCKMORE_HACK_SYNCED`); see `.claude/rules/device-display.md` for the
175	  offset, why it is only valid for a full-frame push, and how to film the
176	  result. Cost: up to a refresh of latency a frame, so only a hack that needs
177	  it should ask.
178	- Budget with `gl_budget.py` but expect it to be off: it has no blend term
179	  (Unknown Pleasures was predicted at 251 ms and ran at 267, then 197 once the
180	  fills were opaque). Add the measured row as a calibration point.
181	- After all that a dimming of about 14% for 25 ms at each push remained (issue
182	  #68). Do not promise a hack is flicker-free from a host frame or from the
183	  absence of vanishing lines alone.
184	
185	## Stack check
186	
187	When: locals over a few KB. Compile the hack with `-O1 -fstack-usage` (flags in
188	AGENTS.md) and keep each frame well under the 16 KB loop stack. Host tests
189	cannot see an overflow: Rorschach's 9.6 KB array rebooted the device on its
190	first frame, and only the serial log's "Stack canary" showed it.
191	
192	Recursion: replay it, don't guess. Run the hack on a pthread with a painted
193	1 MB stack over several seeds and thousands of frames (Pacman's generator: 236
194	KB median, 315 KB worst; `ulimit -s` saw only the first, shallow level). Read a
195	frame's size from the ELF (`xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump -d`, `entry a1, N`), and
196	decode a panic backtrace with `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-addr2line` against an ELF
197	rebuilt with the same flags. A recursion over a grid is bounded by its cells:
198	replay it from every start.
199	
200	## Large allocations
201	
202	When: one allocation of 100 KB or more, or the hack calls `exit()` if it fails.
203	
204	- `unsigned long` is 4 bytes on the device and 8 on the host, so host leak
205	  numbers are double the device's.
206	- Plain `malloc` and `realloc` of two 868 KB buffers (Substrate) landed in
207	  PSRAM: free PSRAM fell by 1,742,096 bytes, which is 2 x 466 x 466 x 4 plus a
208	  few KB. Internal heap barely moved.
209	- On restart the buffers were freed and allocated again, and free PSRAM
210	  returned to the same value. Read heap and PSRAM in the log to confirm this
211	  for each large hack.
212	
213	## Images
214	
215	Colour pixmaps are canvases: every drawing primitive, `XCopyArea` and
216	`XCopyPlane` draw into them. Bitmaps take only `XCopyArea` from another
217	bitmap. There is no PNG
218	decoder: `image_data_to_pixmap` reads a raw RGB565 blob and
219	mask (format in `ximage-loader.h`), made by `tools/make_logo_blob.py`.
220	`XS_LOGO=<image>` (relative to the repository root) swaps the logo for a local
221	image at build time. Keep a third-party logo under `vendor/`, out of git.
222	
223	A big blob (Pacman's is 3 MB as C text) is built from `vendor/` by a `pre:`
224	script and never committed; write it to a `.partial` file and rename it.
225	
226	## Pixmap double buffering
227	
228	When: a plain screenhack makes two pixmaps, draws into them and `XCopyArea`s the
229	result to the window (Anemone, Anemotaxis, Compass, FuzzyFlakes, Halftone,
230	Interaggregate, LMorph, Wormhole). Since #61 this works as copied, but a back
231	buffer costs 434 KB of PSRAM and a full-frame copy each frame, and dirties
232	every row, so the push loses what the dirty rectangle (#52) saves. Draw
233	straight on the canvas instead, as below. (These eight were ported before #61,
234	when the copy from a blank pixmap erased the picture.)
235	
236	- A pinned hash of a blank frame passes silently (`0xa4f79500bd791711ull`, which
237	  is also Pedal's at frame 200). Look at the frame before pinning.
238	- Upstream switches the buffering off under `HAVE_JWXYZ` ("Don't second-guess
239	  Quartz's double-buffering"), or reads a `doubleBuffer` resource. Write
240	  `hacks/<name>_direct.c`: include `screenhack.h` and the math headers, empty
241	  `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE`, `#define HAVE_JWXYZ`, include the unmodified hack and
242	  register its `HackEntry`. Exclude the original from `build_src_filter` in all
243	  three environments. `grep HAVE_JWXYZ` first: Interaggregate also uses it for
244	  pixel packing, but only in the 24 and 32 bit cases, and the canvas is 16 bit.
245	- A hack that uses a pixmap as storage needs no wrapper. Truchet draws a canvas
246	  bigger than the window into an 866 by 866 pixmap (1.5 MB of PSRAM) and
247	  scrolls it with `XCopyArea` offsets.
248	
249	## Restart leak test
250	
251	When: the hack restarts itself. Override its cycle resource in the test (for
252	example `*maxCycles: 3`), compare `__sanitizer_get_current_allocated_bytes()`
253	before and after many restarts, and prove the test sees a leak by removing a
254	`free` in a temporary copy or leaking from a shim function. Never leave the
255	hack changed: `cmp` it afterwards.
256	
257	Measure the growth first, then set the tolerance just above it (Pacman: exactly
258	0, so 512 bytes). A loose one passes a leaked GC; mutation-check by leaking one.
259	
260	On the device, work out how long a restart takes: cycles times the frame time.
261	Substrate's 10,000 cycles at about 160 ms is 27 minutes, and the restart showed
262	at about 25. Capture that long, with `-DROTATE_SECONDS=0`.
263	
264	## Stopping before the first draw
265	
266	When: the hack allocates on its first `draw` (look for a lazy `initted` flag)
267	but sizes its `free` from values set in `init`. Two quick button presses, or a
268	press with the 90 s rotation, free a hack before it has drawn once. Blaster
269	sets `NUM_ROBOTS` in init, allocates `robots` in draw, and its free loops over
270	`robots[i].lasers`, so freeing it first dereferenced NULL. The dump tool with 0
271	frames exited 139.
272	
273	- `test_every_hack_can_be_stopped_before_its_first_frame` starts and stops every
274	  hack with no frame, so a new port that has this problem fails the host suite.
275	- To fix it without editing the hack, write a wrapper that includes the
276	  unmodified source with `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE` emptied and registers the hack
277	  itself, with a `free` that makes the loop safe (`hacks/blaster_safe.c`).
278	- A real press is rarely handled in that window: Rod's presses on the device
279	  all landed after the first step. Rely on the test, not on pressing buttons.
280	- An xlockmore hack cannot be re-registered that way: `xlockmore.h` has no
281	  include guard, so the hack's own include redefines `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE`
282	  after the wrapper empties it. Swap the callback in the table instead, from a
283	  constructor: `<name>_xlockmore_function_table.hack_init = my_init;`
284	  (`loop_direct.c`, `hypnowheel_single_gl.c`).
285	
286	## Tests that cannot be fooled
287	
288	A test that runs a real hack can pass for the wrong reason. Pyro clears its own
289	window in `init`, so a "starts black" test through Pyro passed with the runner
290	deliberately broken. Test shared runner behaviour with stub hacks
291	(`test_runner_xsft.c`) and mutate the code to see the test fail.
292	
293	A check can also be true before the hack has run. "At least 20 non-black
294	pixels" proved a hack drew, until Substrate started on a white canvas and
295	passed without drawing at all. Compare with the canvas as the hack started, and
296	keep a stub hack that draws nothing, on the colour that fooled the old check, to
297	show the test can fail. When a change alters what every hack starts with (the
298	background colour, an initial canvas), re-read the older tests that assume the
299	old start.
300	
301	A bounds guard can be unreachable through the public API. TinyGL's clipper
302	keeps a line inside the view volume and its viewport maps that to at most pixel
303	63.5, so two of the four guards in the smooth-line plot survived mutation until
304	a test used a viewport bigger than the canvas. Mutate each guard on its own
305	(a scratchpad script that edits, runs the suite and restores in `finally`),
306	and when one survives, find an input that reaches it or say it is defensive.
307	Wrapping bugs can also hide in what is stored, not what is drawn: a depth that
308	wrapped round only showed when a third fill was drawn afterwards.
309	
310	## Wrapping an xlockmore hack's init or draw
311	
312	Emptying `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE` (Blaster) fails: the hack includes
313	`xlockmore.h`, which has no include guard and defines it again. Rename the
314	hack's tables instead (`#define pipes_xscreensaver_function_table
315	pipes_upstream_xscreensaver_table`, the same for `_xlockmore_function_table`),
316	include the hack, `#undef` both, define the wrappers, then
317	`#define draw_pipes pipes_draw_no_fade` and call
318	`XSCREENSAVER_MODULE_2("Pipes", pipes, pipes)`. See `hacks/pipes_gl.c`.
319	
320	## Background colour
321	
322	The runner paints the canvas in the hack's `background` resource before `init`,
323	as `screenhack.c` paints the window. Substrate (`.background: white`) depends
324	on it. Every earlier hack asks for black or nothing.
325	
326	## Skipping a hack
327	
328	Threads and shared memory are not worth porting. Record the name and the
329	reason in `tools/failed_ports.txt` (`name: reason`); the scorer marks it as
330	abandoned. Xft text used to be on this list; it is not now (see "Xft text").
331	
332	## Xft text
333	
334	A hack that draws with Xft (`XftDrawStringUtf8`, `load_xft_font_retry`) needs
335	the stand-in in `x11shim/xft.h`. Its font is Special Elite, rasterised at build
336	time into pixel-coverage tables (`firmware/font_atlas.py`, which runs
337	`tools/make_font_atlas.py` on the TTF in `firmware/assets/fonts/`), and
338	`main.cpp` installs it with `xshim_set_font`. Only ASCII has glyphs: anything
339	else draws as `?`. The family in a font name is ignored and the baked size
340	nearest the number is used, so to change a hack's text size override its font
341	resource (XJack's `XJACK_FONT_PX`) and bake the size in `font_atlas.py`.
342	
343	Our `screenhack.h` does not include `xft.h`, because that would change what
344	every hack sees. Build the hack through a wrapper that includes it first
345	(`hacks/xjack_xft.c`), and exclude the original from all three
346	`build_src_filter` lines. XJack's wrapper shows two things an Xft hack may
347	need from `screenhack.c`: the window background set from the `background`
348	resource (`XClearWindow` otherwise clears to black), and a reshape after
349	init. Tests that run the hack install `test_font.h`'s blocky font, so a
350	pinned hash does not follow FreeType; with no font installed the shim gives a
351	blank one, so a test that replays every hack does not abort.
352	
353	## Worktree setup
354	
355	A fresh worktree lacks the ignored `vendor/`, `.venv/` and `.platformio/`:
356	symlink them from the main checkout. They show as untracked, so `git add`
357	named paths, never `-A`. Adding them to `.git/info/exclude` changes state shared
358	with every worktree: ask Rod first.
359	
360	A worktree session refuses `source`, `$VAR` in a command and `&&` chains with a
361	computed path. Run plain commands with literal paths, for example
362	`PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR=<worktree>/.platformio ../.venv/bin/pio test -e native`.
363	
364	## Device capture
365	
366	- Pin the hack with `-DSTART_HACK=\"name\"` and add `-DROTATE_SECONDS=0`, or the
367	  board rotates to the next hack after 90 s.
368	- Send upload output to a file, never through `head`, and look for "Hash of
369	  data verified".
370	- Capture 150 s or more of serial in the background, longer to see a restart.
371	  Read `step`, `push`, `wait`, heap and PSRAM, and any "Stack canary".
372	- Compare with a baseline from the same build, not with old rows: pushes became
373	  41-45 ms on every hack after the byte-order fix, against 31 ms before (#23).
374	- Pinning a frame hash: set the new hack's `kBaseline` entry to `1`, run
375	  `pio test -f test_hacks`, read `Was N` in the failure and convert with
376	  `python3 -c "print('0x%016xull' % N)"`. Pin only after looking at the frame
377	  (and never type the hex by hand: one was wrong).
378	- Showing Rod a hack: flash `-DSTART_HACK=\"first\" -DROTATE_SECONDS=25` with
379	  `XS_LOGO=...` so the new ones come up in order, then tell him which, and that
380	  the button steps backwards (from Pyro it wraps to the last hack).

GUARD = "#ifdef HAVE_AFTER_DARK_TOASTERS\n"


def _guard_in(text: str, start: str, end: str) -> int:
    """Index of GUARD between `start` and `end`, or -1."""
    a = text.find(start)
    b = text.find(end, a)
    if a < 0 or b < 0:
        return -1
    return text.find(GUARD, a, b)


def wire(
    root: Path,
    name: str,
    cls: str,
    copyright_text: str,
    notice: str = "jwz permission notice (above)",
    xlockmore: bool = False,
    glx: bool = False,
) -> None:
    src = root / UPSTREAM / "hacks" / ("glx" if glx else "") / f"{name}.c"
    if not src.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(src)
    dst = root / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / name / f"{name}.c"
    registry = root / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / "registry.c"
    tests = root / "firmware" / "test" / "test_hacks" / "test_hacks.c"
    notices = root / "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"

    reg = registry.read_text()
    if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}_hack\b", reg):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} is already in registry.c")
    if xlockmore:
        decl = f'XLOCKMORE_HACK({name}, "{cls}");\n'
    else:
        decl = f"extern const HackEntry {name}_hack;\n"
    reg = _insert_before(reg, "const HackEntry *const g_hacks[]", decl + "\n")
    g = _guard_in(reg, "g_hacks[] = {", "};")
    if g >= 0:
        reg = reg[:g] + f"    &{name}_hack,\n" + reg[g:]
    else:
        reg, n = re.subn(
            r"    &(\w+)_hack\};", rf"    &\1_hack,\n    &{name}_hack}};", reg, count=1
        )
        if n != 1:
            raise ValueError("cannot find the end of g_hacks[]")

    t = tests.read_text()
    g = _guard_in(t, "expected[] = {", "const int n = sizeof(expected)")
    if g >= 0:
        t = t[:g] + f'                                         "{cls}",\n' + t[g:]
    else:
        t, n = re.subn(
            r'"\};\n  const int n = sizeof\(expected\)',
            f'",\n                                         "{cls}"}};\n  const int n = sizeof(expected)',
            t,
            count=1,
        )
        if n != 1:
            raise ValueError("cannot find the expected list in test_hacks.c")
    g = _guard_in(
        t, "kBaseline[] = {", "void test_frames_of_every_hack_but_maze_match_main"
    )
    if g >= 0:
        t = t[:g] + f"    0, /* {cls}: not yet pinned */\n" + t[g:]
    else:
        t, n = re.subn(
            r"(\};\n\nvoid test_frames_of_every_hack_but_maze_match_main)",
            f"    0, /* {cls}: not yet pinned */\n\\1",
            t,
            count=1,
        )
        if n != 1:
            raise ValueError("cannot find kBaseline in test_hacks.c")
    leak = (
        f"void test_{name}_stops_do_not_leak(void) {{\n"
        f'  check_restarts_and_stops_do_not_leak("{cls}", {1 if xlockmore else 0});\n'
        "}\n\n"
    )
    t = _insert_before(t, "int main(void) {\n  UNITY_BEGIN();", leak)
    t = _insert_before(
        t,
        "  RUN_TEST(test_gears_stack_use_on_the_host_has_not_run_away);\n",
        f"  RUN_TEST(test_{name}_stops_do_not_leak);\n",
    )

    n_text = notices.read_text()
    rows = list(re.finditer(r"\| `firmware/src/hacks/[^\n]*\n", n_text))
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("no hack rows in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md")
    row = f"| `firmware/src/hacks/{name}/{name}.c` | {copyright_text} | {notice} |\n"
    n_text = n_text[: rows[-1].end()] + row + n_text[rows[-1].end() :]

    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy(src, dst)
    registry.write_text(reg)
    tests.write_text(t)
    notices.write_text(n_text)


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.add_argument("cls", metavar="Class")
    p.add_argument("copyright", metavar="copyright")
    p.add_argument("--notice", default="jwz permission notice (above)")
    p.add_argument("--xlockmore", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--glx", action="store_true", help="the source is under hacks/glx/")
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        wire(ROOT, a.name, a.cls, a.copyright, a.notice, a.xlockmore, a.glx)
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
        print(f"wire_hack: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"wired {a.name} ({a.cls}); now fill the shim gaps and run `pio run -e dump`")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

i_log2 (size_t x)
{
  /* -1 works best for to_pow2. */
  if (!x)

  /* GCC 3.4 also has this. */
  /* The preprocessor criteria here must match what's in pow2.h, to prevent

    size_t mask = (size_t)-1;
    unsigned result = bits - 1;

      if (!(x & mask)) {
        result -= bits;
        x <<= bits;
      }

      bits >>= 1;
      mask <<= bits;
    }

    return result;
  }

to_pow2 (size_t x)
{
